I kinda do, but I'm not exactly a recipe cook in that I don't measure things properly. I just add ingredients until what I'm making looks the right consistency and has the right flavor....as you might imagine, I do not do the baking in my home. lol

Anyway, the basic recipe I use is thus:

Whole mustard seeds (I was shocked at how many different kinds of mustard there are. I usually use indian black mustard, personally) This will make up ~90% of the final volume you end up with.

Grind up about a teaspoon worth of whatever seed you're using with your Pestle. The little bit of ground mustard helps immensely with the flavors mingling.

Turmeric (this is what makes mustards yellow, and if you get good quality it adds a fantastic flavor). You can use any number of other spices, though.

a touch of white vinegar

a swirl of honey. I add this is to balance out the bitter flavors found in indian black mustard, but it might not actually necessary for other mustard seeds.

If the mustard is too thick for your liking you can add a little f your favorite minimal flavor cooking oil. I usually use sunflower, but I imagine just about any type would work (don't think I'd recommend peanut or olive, though).

And that's it! Mix these together, wait a few days and see what you've got!

Mustard recipes are as variable as aioli recipes, though! Don't be afraid to experiment!
